text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 — Smart routing fallback loop affecting AcmeCorp chat agents. Symptoms: elevated 5xxs and timeouts for tool_call routes; rolling region fallbacks observed. Pager: @oncall-eric. Initial alert at 2023-11-02T09:12:00Z.

oncall-eric: I'm on it. Can someone paste the top errors and which model variants are involved?

raj: From runtime traces: requests for route `acme-chat-toolcall` were routed to `quant-ggml-eu` (quantized) due to routing policy weight, but this variant does NOT support tool_call. Runtime returned: `error: tool_call_not_supported`. Then smart-router attempted region fallback to `quant-ggml-us`, which also lacks tool_call, then tried `fp16-us` but routing policy capped that due to cost tier => oscillation. Snippet from logs:

```
ERROR request_id=abcd1234 model=quant-ggml-eu route=acme-chat-toolcall status=422 err=tool_call_not_supported
WARN smart-router request_id=abcd1234 action=fallback target=quant-ggml-us
ERROR smart-router request_id=abcd1234 action=fallback target=fp16-us reason=quota_capped
```

sam: We're seeing the fallback loop in metrics — spike in retries and token latency. Query (approx): `sum(rate(router.fallbacks[1m])) by (route)` shows ~120 fallbacks/minute for `acme-chat-toolcall`. Also a correlated increase in 5xxs from the serving runtime.

tess: I pulled the compatibility matrix entry for `quant-ggml-*` variants — it incorrectly has `tool_call: true` and `max_context: 8192`. The actual build only supports `tool_call: false` and `max_context: 2048` (we regressed when we merged the quant matrix PR last week). That mismatch is what's letting smart-router choose quant variants for tool_call-enabled routes.

neha: Customer impact: AcmeCorp reports intermittent 500s for their chat widget. They estimated ~6k requests affected in the last 20 minutes. On the record: partial outage for tool-calling flows.

raj: Proposed immediate mitigation (short-term): 1) Update routing policy to exclude quant variants for any route with `requires_tool_call=true` (hotpatch). 2) Add runtime guard so attempts to send tool_call to a variant with `tool_call=false` are rejected locally (fast fail) and trigger fallback to next compatible variant. 3) Fix compatibility matrix entry and roll forward.

raj: Hotpatch command to update policy via control-plane API:

```
# prefer fp16 for tool_call routes
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/policies/hotpatch" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"route":"acme-chat-toolcall","policy":{"preferred_variants":["fp16-*"],"exclude_tags":["quant"]}}'
```

oncall-eric: Running the hotpatch now.

deploy-bot: deploy:policy-hotpatch started by oncall-eric (run id=deploy-789)

oncall-eric: Hotpatch applied, control-plane returned 200.

raj: Pushing runtime guard to serving (non-disruptive): will return 422 for any request that sets `tool_call` true but attempts to use a model with `tool_call=false`. Command to rollout small canary:

```
kubectl -n runtime set image deploy/serve runtime=serve:guard-20231102-canary
```

eng-sre-bot: canary rollout succeeded on 2 nodes; health checks pass.

sam: Monitoring: fallback rate for `acme-chat-toolcall` dropped from 120/min to 3/min within 90s of hotpatch. Error budget burn stopped. Graphs show 5xxs trending back to baseline. :white_check_mark:

tess: Created PR to correct compatibility matrix (https://git.internal/redwood/compat-matrix/pull/452). Patch changes: `quant-ggml-*: tool_call: false, max_context: 2048, note: "Quantized builds trim some ops; no tool calling"`. Adding an integration test to detect mismatch between stated matrix and actual variant capabilities.

neha: I'll draft a customer-facing status update for AcmeCorp — will include that we applied a routing hotpatch and are rolling a fix to the compatibility data to prevent recurrence. DM me the contact and I’ll send.

product-ops-bot: Suggested status blurb:

"We experienced degraded responses for tool-calling chat flows. Engineers applied a routing hotpatch to prevent incompatible model variants from being selected and rolled a non-disruptive runtime guard. We are deploying a permanent fix to the model compatibility data and will follow up with a postmortem."

oncall-eric: Sent update to Acme support channel. Customer acknowledged and said impact reduced; requested postmortem.

raj: Follow-ups (post-incident actions):
- ship compatibility matrix fix (PR #452) and verify with integration test
- add preflight check in smart-router: `variant.capabilities` vs `route.requirements` before selection
- add public telemetry: `router.selection_mismatch` metric to catch future mismatches early
- add unit test in model-onboarding CI to assert `tool_call` capability is accurate

sam: Filing incident ticket INC-2023-759 in tracker, assigning to eng-runtime + eng-platform for root cause and remediation tracking.

eng-sre-bot: Alert: Incident annotated as `resolved` by oncall-eric at 2023-11-02T09:27:05Z. Duration ~15m.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> Resolved. Postmortem owner: raj. Please file a postmortem within 72 hours and tag #incidents. :memo:

product-ops-bot: Noted. I'll coordinate customer follow-up and schedule a sync with AcmeCorp for timeline on mitigations.

neha: Thanks all. Good catch on the matrix regression. We'll tighten review for matrix changes.

oncall-eric: Closing thread. Good job team. :trophy:
